key_insight: HTP-Net improves instance segmentation of dense welding-material stubs by preserving fine boundaries, maintaining slender-target connectivity, and separating overlapping instances.
engineering_relevance: More reliable stub counting and shape measurement can support automated inventory management in welding factories.
method: Wavelet-driven edge preservation retains subtle boundaries during downsampling.
Long-range topology modeling reduces fragmentation of slender targets.
An orientation-driven segmentation head uses rotational priors to reduce excessive suppression and overlapping masks.
evidence_signal: Across custom and public dense-slender-material datasets, the abstract reports mAP50 improvements of 1.2%–55.3%; factory validation achieved average recognition accuracies of 99% for electrode stubs and 94% for wire stubs.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, runtime, or recognition-accuracy definitions, limiting assessment of deployment scalability and generalization.
paper_title: High-resolution topology-preserving instance segmentation network for vision-based measurement system of dense welding material stubs
